app.title: VPN55 admin
app.noscript: This page needs JavaScript. Turn it on for this site and reload.
app.waiting: Waiting for the first reading from the services.
app.readonly: This build can only read. Nothing on this page changes anything on the server.
app.source: The server's own configuration is the source of truth. Everything here is read from the services on each refresh, not stored by this panel.
app.unreachable.title: The panel itself is not answering
app.unreachable.body: The browser could not reach this panel. What is shown below is the last reading it received, and it is not being updated.
overview.title: Is anything wrong right now
overview.allwell: Nothing needs attention. Every service is running, no service has raised a warning, every credential belongs to a user in the registry, and nobody is over quota or expired.
overview.unknown.waiting: No reading has arrived from the services yet, so this screen cannot answer the question. It will as soon as the first poll succeeds.
overview.unknown.stale: The last few readings failed, so what is below is not current and this screen cannot say whether anything is wrong. The banner above says when the last good reading was.
overview.service.unavailable: {service} could not be reached at all. The panel cannot say anything about it, including whether anyone is connected through it.
overview.service.bootdisabled: {service} is running but is not set to start at boot. It will not come back after a reboot.
overview.orphans: {count} credential(s) are being served to a user who is not in the registry. Removing the user will not remove them.
overview.expired: {count} user(s) have passed their expiry date.
overview.expiry.unparseable: {count} user(s) have an expiry date this panel cannot read, so it does not know whether they have expired.
value.unknown.help: The service keeps no record of this. It is not the same as never — it means there is nothing to read.
value.never.help: The service does keep this record, and it says this has not happened.
value.noreading.help: No reading. The service could not answer, so this is blank rather than zero.
service.unavailable.help: This service cannot run on this host — its software is missing or this system does not support it.
service.boot.disabled.help: It is running now but will not start again after a reboot.
services.none: No services are configured on this host.
filtering.label: On a filtered network
filtering.level.unrecognised: This panel does not recognise that answer. Read the service's own explanation below rather than the label above.
custody.label: Who holds the key
revoke.label: When access is withdrawn
revoke.latency.crl: Takes effect when the block list is next read
revoke.unbounded: No guaranteed limit — a session already open may continue indefinitely.
revoke.worstcase: At worst {duration} before it takes effect.
restart.label: If this service is restarted
note.severity.unrecognised: This panel does not recognise that level, so it is shown at the loudest one.
fromservice.label: From the service:
fromservice.help: These are the service's own words, passed through unchanged. This panel cannot translate them, so they stay in the language the service wrote them in.
users.none: No users have been created yet.
users.col.name: Name
users.col.creds.help: Total credentials, with the number currently connected in brackets.
user.disabled.help: This user is blocked from connecting. Their credentials still exist.
quota.unlimited.help: This user has no quota set. That is not the same as a quota of zero.
expiry.never.help: No expiry date is set for this user.
orphans.title: Credentials with no user
orphans.explain: The services are serving these credentials, but the user register does not list who they belong to. That should not happen: the register is meant to be the complete list. Until it is resolved, nobody is accountable for this traffic.
orphans.nouser.help: The service did not say which user this belongs to.
connections.explain: Credentials the services reported a current remote address for on the last reading.
conn.col.endpoint.help: The remote address this person is connecting from. It is read live and is not stored by this panel.
conn.mask.state.on: Remote addresses are shortened to their network.
conn.mask.state.off: Remote addresses are shown in full.
conn.mask.help: Shortens each remote address to its network — the first three parts of an IPv4 address, the first three groups of an IPv6 one. This changes what is on this screen only: the panel does not store remote addresses either way.
conn.mask.unmaskable: Hidden. This value is not an address this panel knows how to shorten, so it is not shown while addresses are masked. Use Show addresses to read it.
conn.col.endpoint.masked.help: The network this person is connecting from, not their full address. It is read live and is not stored by this panel.
conn.col.session.help: Down / up since this session started. Every service resets these — on a restart, on a reconnection, or on a key change — so they go backwards and are not a usage total.
conn.col.total.help: Down / up added up across every session, kept by this panel because no service can answer it. This is the number that means usage.
conn.resets.help: How many times this credential's counters have gone backwards and been carried into the accumulated total.
event.counter.reset: {service}: counters for {user} restarted — {carried} carried into their total
event.cred.vanished: {service}: the credential {cred} for {user} is no longer served
event.status.unreadable: The services could not be read ({kind})
event.status.recovered: The services can be read again, after {failures} failed attempts
event.record.unknown: A service sent {count} record(s) of a kind this panel does not know: {type}
health.stale.title: These numbers are out of date
health.stale.body: The last successful reading was {when}. {failures} attempts have failed since. Everything below is from that reading and is not being updated.
health.never.body: The services have never been read successfully. {failures} attempts have failed. Nothing below can be trusted.
health.kind.missing: The program that reads the services is not where it is configured to be.
health.kind.permission: Permission was refused. The panel is not allowed to run the read.
health.kind.timeout: The read did not finish in time.
health.kind.empty: The read succeeded but returned nothing at all, which is not a valid answer.
auth.title: Sign in
auth.bad_credentials: That name and password do not match.
auth.locked: Too many failed attempts for this name from this address. Try again in {minutes} minutes.
auth.rate_limited: Too many sign-in attempts from this address. Try again in {minutes} minutes.
auth.csrf_failed: That request did not carry this session's token, so it was refused. Reload the page and try again.
auth.expired: The session ended. Sign in again.
auth.idle_warning: This session ends in {seconds} seconds unless you do something.
auth.off.title: Sign-in is switched off
auth.off.body: allow_unauthenticated is set. Everyone who can reach this address can read everything here AND change it. Set it to 0 in panel.conf.
auth.totp.help: The six-digit code your authenticator app is showing.
auth.totp_required: This account also needs a code from its authenticator app.
auth.totp_invalid: That code is not right. Wait for the next one and try again.
auth.totp_reused: That code has already been used. Wait for the next one.
auth.totp_enrol_required: This panel requires a second factor and this account has none. It has to be enrolled at the console, as root.
action.rate_limited: Refreshing too often. Try again in a moment.
user.invalid_name: A name is 2 to 32 characters: a lowercase letter first, then a-z 0-9 _ and -.
user.remove.confirm: Delete {name}? Their record goes; nothing they hold is revoked by this.
user.remove.blocked: {name} still holds working credentials. Revoke those first, because deleting the record would leave access on this server with nobody accountable for it.
user.disable.partial: {name} is disabled, and {count} of their credentials still carry traffic. Disabling stops new credentials being issued; it does not end a tunnel that is already up. Revoke those credentials to cut access.
user.field.quota.help: Leave blank for unlimited. Blank is not zero, and zero would mean no traffic at all.
cred.invalid_id: That is not a credential id.
cred.revoke.done.immediate: {cred} is revoked, and that device is off the tunnel now.
cred.revoke.done.delayed: {cred} is revoked. It cannot reconnect; a session it already has may continue.
cred.revoke.confirm: Revoke {cred}? It cannot be restored, and that person will need a new credential.
service.invalid_tag: That is not a service this panel manages.
service.restart.failed: {service} did not come back up. Give it a moment and refresh; if it is still down, read that service’s journal on the host.
audit.title: What has been changed
audit.second_log: The privileged helper keeps its own copy of this log, which this panel cannot write. If the two ever disagree, that one is the record.
enforce.title: Quota and expiry
enforce.off: Enforcement is switched off in the configuration.
enforce.quota_window_reset: Back under quota, because the window rolled over.
enforce.registry_unreadable: The user list could not be read, so nothing was checked.
enforce.stillconnected: {count} disabled account(s) still hold working credentials. Disabling is a policy flag; it does not end a tunnel that is already up.
enforce.quotaskipped: {count} account(s) with a quota had no usage reading and were not checked. A missing reading is not a zero.
enforce.revoke.on: Credentials are revoked automatically when this job disables an account.
enforce.revoke.off: Credentials are NOT revoked automatically. Revoking cannot be undone, so it stays off until you turn it on.
portal.title: VPN55 account
portal.signin.title: Sign in
portal.signin.help: Paste the access code you were sent. If you opened a link, this happens on its own.
portal.state.disabled.help: Your account has been switched off. Your configurations still exist.
portal.disabled.explain: Your account is switched off, so no new configuration can be issued. A connection that is already up is not cut by this — none of these services can suspend access and later restore it.
portal.notconnected.help: This device is not connected right now. The configuration still works.
portal.nokillswitch.title: If the VPN drops, your traffic is not blocked
portal.nokillswitch.body: When the VPN connection drops, your device goes back to the ordinary network and your traffic keeps flowing — it is simply no longer protected. Nothing blocks it automatically. Before doing anything that needs to stay private, check that your VPN app still shows connected. If it has disconnected, stop and reconnect before carrying on.
portal.nokillswitch.short: If the VPN drops, your traffic keeps flowing over the ordinary network, unprotected. Check that the app still shows connected.
portal.rotate.confirm: Replace your {service} configuration? The new one is issued first and the old one then stops working, so the device using it now will need the new file.
portal.rotate.done: Replaced. Use the new configuration; the old one no longer works.
portal.rotate.partial: The new configuration was issued, but the old one could not be withdrawn and still works. Tell whoever runs this server.
portal.rotate.already: This configuration is no longer on your account — it may already have been replaced. The list has been refreshed.
portal.rotate_failed_kept: The new configuration could not be issued, so nothing changed. The one you have still works.
portal.config.gone: The file for this one is no longer on the server. The key inside it was erased after it was issued, which is deliberate. Use Replace to get a new one.
portal.qr.label: Configuration as a QR code
portal.qr.help: Scan this with the app on your phone.
portal.qr.toobig: This file is too large for a QR code. Save it and open it in the app instead.
portal.copy.failed: Could not copy. Select the text and copy it by hand.
portal.binary: This file is not text. Save it and open it with the app it is for.
portal.nocreds.title: Nothing has been issued to you yet
portal.nocreds.body: Ask whoever runs this server to issue you a configuration.
portal.stale.title: These figures are out of date
portal.stale.body: The services could not be read on the last attempt. What is shown comes from the last reading that worked.
portal.bad_code: That code does not work. It may have been withdrawn, or it may have expired. Ask whoever runs this server for a new one.
portal.rate_limited: Too many attempts from this address. Try again in {minutes} minutes.
portal.rotate_limited: You have replaced this too many times recently. Try again in {minutes} minutes.
portal.csrf_failed: That request did not carry this session's token, so it was refused. Reload the page and try again.
portal.cred_unknown: That configuration is not one of yours.
portal.not_ready: The services have not been read yet. Try again in a moment.
portal.no_account: This account no longer exists on this server. Ask whoever runs it whether you should still have access.
portal.artifact_unknown: That is not a file this configuration has.
portal.failed: That did not work. Try again, and if it keeps happening tell whoever runs this server.
portal.unreachable: Could not reach the server. Check your connection and try again.
portal.not_found: There is nothing here. Open your account page, or follow the link you were sent again.
portal.disabled: The self-serve portal is switched off on this server.
portal.token.title: Portal access
portal.token.none: No access codes have been issued.
portal.token.revoke.confirm: Withdraw this access code? Whoever holds it is signed out and will need a new one.
portal.token.once: This is the only time this code is shown. It is not stored and cannot be shown again — withdraw it and issue another if it goes astray.
portal.token.label: Label (optional)
portal.token.col.label: Label
portal.token.bad_days: The number of days must be a whole number from 1 to 3650.
portal.token.invalid_id: That is not the id of an access code.
portal.token.unknown: There is no access code with that id.
settings.intro: These change how the panel behaves. Every one of them takes effect at once — nothing here needs a restart.
settings.sshonly: Everything else stays in {file} and can only be changed over SSH: the sign-in switch, the second-factor requirement, the addresses this panel listens on, whether a proxy header is believed, the paths of the two programs it asks root to run, the two switches that revoke credentials, and where alerts are sent.
settings.stored: Changes are stored in {file}. Nothing here is written to the settings file above, which stays owned by root.
settings.source.panel.help: This value was set on this screen and is overriding the settings file. Editing that file will not change it until you choose "Use the file".
settings.unavailable: Settings are not available on this panel.
settings.unknown_key: This panel does not expose that setting.
settings.invalid_value: That value is outside what this setting allows. The permitted range is shown under the field.
settings.key.poll_seconds: How often to read the services
settings.key.poll_seconds.help: Seconds between readings. Every reading is one command on this host, and it is also how fresh every number on these pages is.
settings.key.event_limit.help: How many entries the Events page holds. Older ones are dropped as new ones arrive.
settings.key.log_level.help: What this panel writes to the system journal.
settings.key.default_locale.help: The language for anyone who has not chosen one. Each person’s own choice still wins.
settings.key.session_ttl_minutes.help: Minutes before a session ends however active it is. It is capped at 24 hours in code, which no setting can raise.
settings.key.session_idle_minutes.help: Minutes of no activity before a session ends. Looking at a page is not activity; only doing something is.
settings.key.login_window_ms.help: Milliseconds. The period the two counts below are measured over.
settings.key.login_max_failures.help: Wrong passwords and wrong codes, counted for one name from one address together.
settings.key.login_lock_ms.help: Milliseconds that a locked-out name and address must wait.
settings.key.login_ip_max.help: Every sign-in attempt from one address, whatever name is tried.
settings.key.enforce_enabled.help: Whether the periodic job runs at all. What it is allowed to do when it finds something is set over SSH, because revoking cannot be undone.
settings.key.alert_confirmations.help: How many readings in a row must agree before a condition is announced — and before it is called over. Two absorbs a single bad reading.
settings.key.alert_cooldown_seconds.help: Seconds. The same condition is not announced twice inside this, however many times it changes.
settings.key.alert_max_per_hour.help: A ceiling under everything else. If it is being reached, one of the two settings above is wrong for this host.
settings.key.alert_status_failures.help: How many readings must fail in a row before the panel announces that it cannot see this host.
alerts.state.unconfigured: Alerts are on, but nowhere to send them is set, so nothing is sent.
alerts.sent: {count} sent in the last hour, out of {max}.
alerts.lasterror: The last attempt to send did not work:
alert.status.unreadable.title: VPN55: this host cannot be read
alert.status.unreadable.body: Reading the services has failed {count} times in a row. Nothing else this panel reports is current while that is true.
alert.status.unreadable.clear.title: VPN55: this host can be read again
alert.enforce.still_connected.title: VPN55: disabled accounts are still connected
alert.enforce.still_connected.body: {count} account(s) this panel disabled still hold working credentials. Disabling is a policy flag; it does not end a tunnel that is already up.
alert.enforce.still_connected.clear.titl: VPN55: no disabled account is still connected
alert.enforce.still_connected.clear.body: Every account this panel disabled has now disconnected.
alert.enforce.quota_skipped.title: VPN55: quotas are not being checked
alert.enforce.quota_skipped.body: {count} account(s) with a quota have no usage reading, so their quota was not checked. A missing reading is not a zero.
alert.enforce.quota_skipped.clear.title: VPN55: quotas are being checked again
alert.enforce.quota_skipped.clear.body: Every account with a quota now has a usage reading.
alert.enforce.baselines_reset.title: VPN55: usage totals went backwards
alert.enforce.baselines_reset.body: {count} quota baseline(s) were taken again, because a lifetime total was lower than its own baseline. The stored totals were lost or restored from an older copy, and this window under-reports.
alert.auth.locked_out.title: VPN55: sign-in lockout
alert.auth.locked_out.body: {count} sign-in lockout(s) have been triggered on the panel. The audit log on the host has the names and the addresses; this message deliberately does not.
